utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning. This is Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before we continue the examination of Witness DP4, there are two pending issues on which the parties asked a decision of the Chamber. First there is the issue whether the summaries provided by Defence are of sufficient precision. In general terms, the summaries are precise enough. That means if, for example, it stated in the summary that the witness will testify about the confrontation lines where he was at, it needs not further specification as to say exactly near to his position, the confrontation lines were on these and these streets or these and these buildings. So in general terms the summaries are specific enough. The second issue is that we, the Chamber and the Prosecution has not been provided with all the, I would say, extended summaries, because the initial summaries were insufficient, and, therefore, we received some six, seven, or eight extended summaries. And when I said that the summaries were specific enough, I was talking about these extended summaries, but they are available only in respect of a small number of witnesses. And as the Chamber indicated before, they have to be provided at a very short notice for all the witnesses that will be called. If the Prosecution feels that in a specific -- on a specific issue the summary is not precise enough, the first thing the Prosecution would have to do is to ask for further details to the Defence. And if this would not solve the problem, the Prosecution may address the Chamber. That is also one of the reasons why the Defence really has to provide these summaries soon now so that the Prosecution, while preparing its cross-examination, can find out whether it contains, in the view of the Prosecution, sufficient information. If not, that they can ask for additional information to the Defence, and if this is not provided, the Prosecution can address the Chamber. The Chamber can decide on whether further more specific information should be contained in the summary. Finally, I said before that in general terms the summaries were specific enough. Where the summaries refer to specific incidents, especially the scheduled incidents, and where the summaries say that the witness will testify on the relevant facts related to that incident, there it is not clear what these relevant facts are. Sometimes the words used say on the basis of the foregoing, and then we have some general information. This information is relevant for specific sniping incidents. The Chamber understands this as to mean that this general information might be of relevance for assessing what happened at specific incidents. Sometimes the words are used that the witness will testify on relevant facts in relation to certain incidents. There it has to be clear what these facts are. Let me just try to give you an example. If, for example, the Defence expects the witness to testify on the line of view from certain positions to the place where someone was hit by a bullet, then it should be clear that that is -- that these are the facts. It could be a different thing. It could, for example, be that a relevant fact might be that one of the incidents that the Defence has spotted someone who, by accident, fired a weapon. That is a totally different but might be relevant fact or an investigation has shown that no shots were fired from the positions where the Prosecution says that from that position a fire came and the investigation has shown that there was no one at this position during three days. That is -- so it should be clear what kind of relevant facts the witness will testify about in relation to specific incidents. That is as far as the summaries is concerned. Then the second issue we dealt with yesterday was about questions inviting a witness to speculate on certain aspects. In cases like these, one cannot always avoid to ask a witness to draw conclusions within his specific knowledge based on his specific experience. But it should be clear that first this knowledge has to be established before a witness can be invited to draw whatever conclusion or to tell us what on the basis of his experience could have been the case. So, therefore the knowledge of the witness first has to be established. And second, it should be perfectly clear on the basis of what experience and on the basis of what facts the witness comes to certain conclusions. For example, if a witness would be asked to tell us whether damage was done intentionally or by firing errors, it should be first established before you can ask such a question to a witness what he knows about specific weaponry, what he knows about the margin of error, what actually he observed that caused him to believe that it was either an error or specifically not an error. So we first need to establish experience, knowledge, facts, and only then we might come to whatever conclusions. Otherwise, such conclusions as we all know that witnesses are mainly witnesses of facts, but sometimes on the basis of their experience within a limited area they could draw some conclusions. We should avoid that it becomes mere speculations because speculation does not assist the Chamber in making the determinations it will have to make. These are the two issues that were still pending. And, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you are on your feet. I know that the witness is standby waiting outside. So if there is any observation you have to make at this moment, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly. Your Honour, thank you, first of all. And regarding this issue, the witness issue. I do not think that Mr. Ierace will contradict me because he received two letters that I sent last night. But unfortunately for some -- because of the time constraint, it is impossible for us to furnish this extended summary for all the witnesses. What we propose to do is that we submitted our witness to two grids of questioning. First of all, Ms. Pilipovic is -- was asking these questions and secondly, there was a cross -- criss-crossed questioning and so we asked some questions of that saw it last night and around 11 p.m. I believe, we made sure to send to the Prosecution what we had -- we simply discovered it was a letter representing a supplementary complementary letter. I do not believe that Mr. Ierace can say something against it. So this is what we decided to do. That was one observation. And secondly, regarding your decision, we thank you for your decision, but the Defence would like to underline the following: Is that during the trial during the prosecution case, they often asked witnesses if they witnessed some firing and if they were present during some random shelling. We have seen that very often these witnesses did not know where these places were situated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, of course, the Chamber has taken into consideration what happened during the Prosecution case. It is not at this moment in time to comment specifically. If there are any further submissions to be made in this respect, it can be done at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then the Chamber has noticed that the Defence indicates that it cannot provide the more extended summaries for all of the witnesses. The Chamber will consider, because there was, I think, an oral order that it had to be done on short notice, and I think it would have been appropriate to inform the Chamber, but perhaps this is the information the Defence now gives the Chamber, that they cannot do it. We will consider whether the existing order will be replaced or mitigated or changed after the Prosecution has been in the position to give its view on that. I would now like to -- unless there is something that should be dealt with at this very moment before the witness comes in. So that it Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. is relevant for this witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I must say that sometimes we can discover certain things, and that is why I am saying, we at times discover very important facts. We have discovered for instance, last night and I can say it now that this very famous tall building that we were talking about, which was situated in Dobrinja was not usable to shoot from. We discovered this only a few hours ago. The second examination that we submitted our witness to reveal this, and we shall apply it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The disclosure of statements and the summaries of witness statements is intended to prevent trial by ambush. The Chamber is aware that sometimes at a later stage surprises come up, but we have to consider whether it is acceptable that new facts come up always or frequently the day before the examination of the witness but we will have to give this further consideration. It is also a matter of case preparation. Mr. Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the Defence is ready to continue the examination, they may do so. And may I remind you, Mr. DP4, that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Witness, good morning, once again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you come close to the microphones. I have a feeling that we cannot hear you very well. Thank you. Very well. Witness, I would be -- I would appreciate it very much if you would be able to answer shortly. If you could just say yes or no, that would help us greatly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, have you personally while you were a soldier, have you personally seen shelling? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Have you personally witnessed shellings that took place on Nedzarici, in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now, regarding your own experience, could you please tell this Chamber if you can if those shellings were frequent, rare, numerous, or something else? What can you tell us? How can you describe those shellings, according to your own experience?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were numerous.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Now, these shellings, sir, were they targeting some very precise military or -- pardon -- objectives or were they directed towards all the Nedzarici neighbourhood, according to your own experience, of course?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President. That is not something that the witness could possibly respond to on the basis of his personal knowledge. I say that given the evidence in relation to this witness so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think this should not be too much of a -- Mr. DP4, may I ask you the following? Did you observe that specific buildings were more frequently hit or were hit at all while others were not, or while observing the shelling, could you see no distinction in buildings being hit or not being hit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the buildings that were hit were the buildings on a larger area. So it is not the same buildings on many occasions but rather various buildings. It is a very small neighbourhood, and it is not difficult to see where the shell fell if it is not right next to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But the question was not whether the was difficult to see but for example, if I say were shops were hit than houses or were your headquarters of the military hit more shops or tall buildings more than small buildings? Or was there any -- could you make any -- could you see any difference in the type of buildings that were hit or the frequency with which some constructions were hit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I was not able to see a difference. And if I may I will explain, if you allow me to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall give you an example. For instance, there was a building called Samo Stan and it's actually the convent. It is a building of a few floors. I cannot say that it's a very tall building, but it consists of a few floors. And the houses that are situated around this convent were hit more often than the convent itself. So I cannot say they were targeting those houses or were they maybe targeting the convent but they were not able so they hit the houses. But I will give you a few examples. My house for instance was hit and in front of the house two shells had fell. On the first time a mother died. She was the victim of this incident. And on the second occasion my aunt was wounded. Now, the house right next to my house -- I don't want to give you any names unless we go perhaps in closed session -- right, so the house right next to mine was hit by a Howitzer shell. And just -- it was like an old villa. It was situated across the street from the convent, and it was hit on a few occasions by mortars. The people who used to live there had gone to live somewhere else and they also owned a house not far from that one. So there were no casualties. That house did not -- was not used for military installation or anything like that. Now the house that was on the same side, on the same side as the convent on the street Aleja Bosne Srebrene was hit as well. It was a mortar hit. And the garden that was situated behind the house was also hit by a very heavy weaponry which had a very great destruction power. And those shells were thrown from the bottom, from the foot of the Mount Igman in the direction of Hrasnica. This is why I am telling you that I cannot tell you what they wished to do, what the Muslim forces tried to target but these were the houses and these were the targets that were targeted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I stop you there --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the intersection was also hit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, your answer was clear. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, as you might have noticed, I asked for facts. The witness explained what he has seen. Please proceed and keep in mind the answer of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness just one observation. In the transcript we could read that a mother died. It was your mother who died, if I am not mistaken? Can you please be more precise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was my mother. She died.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, let's pursue this line of questioning, Witness. During your war experience, were you ever able to see the weapon called a mortar? Have you ever seen a mortar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Did you have the opportunity to discuss with your soldiers this type of weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you therefore, know from your personal experience if this type of weapon implies the possibility of error when it is used? I mean, error in targeting?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, again, no proper basis has been established to ask that question. To save time, could I simply make this observation: I understand that in due course the Defence will be calling Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. an expert and that is the way to deal with this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, may I be heard?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This witness has quoted a number of examples of destruction which took place and knew something that he call as convent, a monastery --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... in the presence of the witness. I will put a few questions to the witness. Mr. DP4 do you have specific technical knowledge on the weapons just mentioned to you, mortars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not an expert. All I can say is what I either saw or went through. If you want to mean -- when our side fired shots we were warned to get away, if possible, in case to avoid casualties on our side when firing. So they were afraid of errors, but I can't say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like you to respond to my questions and these will be very specific questions. Do you have any experience in firing mortars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were you ever given theoretical training in the use of mortars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any specific knowledge of the margin of errors when firing mortars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. But I can give you examples of errors that I know about, errors committed -- made by artillery weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you give me one example, I will then see whether there are any additional questions to be put to you in respect of that example.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will quote to you the example, which, to my mind, was not deliberate because it happened to the French Battalion during rapid intervention. On that occasion an artillery weapon, an artillery projectile hit in front of -- hit the Zica hospital. And in this vicinity there are neither military nor even civilian structures. Since the French Battalion certainly did not intend to do it, I guess it was a calculation error or something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is a conclusion. You were not present when the -- this projectile hit in front of the hospital? Is this what you heard, what other people told you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, on that occasion, two men, two people were killed, Mr. And Mrs. Knezevic. I know their son, Zeljko Knezevic who for a while was deployed in Nedzarici. I attended their funeral.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you. I do understand that you knew persons that were victims of this mortar firing. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You told us that since the French Battalion certainly would not have targeted a hospital, it must have been a firing error. Do you know what the French hospital -- the French Battalion targeted when they fired the shell that finally landed near the hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is assumed that the French Battalion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you. I would like to ask you whether you know personally or not, I mean, what you heard from other people or what can be assumed is a different matter. Do you have --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I do not have such knowledge, not any positive knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you have any specific experience which would allow you to make a distinction between shells that landed as a result of a firing error or shells that landed specifically on the spot targeted by those who fired that shell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that some shells fired from our weapons hit our targets, and I think that those must have been firing errors.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just see whether I understand you well. You say that caused by firing errors your own shells did hit targets in an area controlled by your own armed forces? Is that -- so, by accident you did hit your own positions or people's or objects? Is that how I am to understand your last answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you gave this answer, is it about mortars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was the most frequently the case, mortars, because they were the most widely used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do I understand since you have no experience in firing mortars yourself, that this is what you heard from your colleagues, that they hit targets within the territory controlled by your forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard that from my colleagues who had been barely missed, who could have been killed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Were you informed about what was targeted and what was hit or were you just informed that your own positions were hit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we were not informed about what the actual target was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed and keep in mind the -- to what extent the witness has knowledge and experience on which he could draw any inferences.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, Mr. President. But the Defence takes the liberty of noting for the transcript that one of the questions that you asked seemed practically impossible to answer. It is the question of -- which had to do about the difference between firing error and targeting -- and hitting a particular target. Because it is impossible to answer such a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, could you please indicate to what question you are referring.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but I have to look it up, I have to look at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it page 13, line 9 or 8?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will check it, Mr. President. Yes, it is the question on page 13, line 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I asked the witness about experience not about distinction to be made. I asked him whether he had specific experience that would allow him. Please proceed. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, in one of your answers that you gave now you said that when there was firing you would be warned to leave certain areas, that is what you said. Why were you told to leave certain areas? Will you tell us that please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so as to best take care of the lives of our men in the area of a possible error. I guess that would be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, did you ever hear in Sarajevo from the other side of the line about the use of sirens that is, of -- sounding the alert?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, I would like to go back to the destruction in Nedzarici. Can you tell us, if you can of course, how many houses approximately remained intact in Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object Mr. President. Perhaps my learned colleague could indicate by which time, having regard to the indictment period.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this objection needs to be denied because we know well that this witness was there throughout the war. And I am asking him a question from September 1992 until the end of the war, and, therefore, we are talking about the years that we know very well. So there is absolutely no need for this Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. objection because it is only wasting the time that the Defence has.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The objection is denied. The question was: "How many houses remained intact?" And that is the situation, I would say, at the end of your observation whether there were still -- how many houses were still there that were not -- that remained intact, were not damaged? You may answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The area that we are talking about is very small, and it is surrounded by tall buildings. So all the buildings were hit by different weapons. There were no houses that had not been hit at least from infantry weapons, if nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And as for mortar hits or other types of shells, projectiles of this kind?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same applies.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Let us try to be precise. In time you were in this war from the beginning. This destruction, did it happen mostly, for instance towards the end of 1994 that is towards the end of autumn, in autumn, or did it happen at some other time, at the beginning of the war or some halfway through the war? I don't know. I am talking about the main -- the chief destruction.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chief destruction approximately took place between the end and mid-1992 or end of 1992 until the end of the war. So it was only at the very beginning of the war that they mostly applied infantry attacks. But later on they changed their method.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, we shall now move on to a different set of questions. Did you receive any instructions concerning the objects that you could target or specifically did your company receive -- or perhaps it didn't, I do not know -- receive any instructions concerning the types of targets that you were right in taking on? Please answer with yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And what were the instructions that you received?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The instructions were: Return the fire, take care not to target civilians, women, children.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You stopped here. You told us not to target civilians, women, and children. By "civilians," do you also include the elderly amongst these civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the unarmed and un-uniformed individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And were those instructions sent to you through the channel -- chain of command?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We received the instructions from the company commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. I am re-reading the transcript. I believe that you said, to make it quite specific that you received them from the company command. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But that is not the same thing as the "command chain." Do you know where did your company command receive its instructions from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The company command received its instructions from the battalion command, and they were receiving their instructions from the brigade command. I am not familiar with the chain of command further up.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Witness, I would like you now to be shown a map which has the number, it is the map of the incident number 23.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And we have copied this and we would like to give these copies -- to distribute these copies. Excuse me just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a set which was supplied -- which was shown to a witness who was a Corps Commander. And whilst this document is being distributed --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, can you confirm that what you just called "the convent" or the monastery, at times it's the same building, is the building which is at times called the School of Theology.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is one and the same building.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you have before you -- you have before you a map. Can you -- you read this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us, according to you, which is -- what is the building which is next to number 75?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the School of Theology.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, perhaps the usher could help us. [In English] On the ELMO. Would you please put it on the ELMO. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May it then be put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There. Thank you. For the transcript this is Exhibit P3728, but we have produced a copy, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you see a point to the -- on the right-hand side of the map towards 23, with a kind of an arrow pointing at 23?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You have this red triangle before you and it literally represents the firing trajectory, that is the theoretical possibility of a shot coming from the School of Theology and being fired at point 23. Having said that, and in view of your knowledge of the area was it technically possible, according to your experience to effect one shot from point indicated towards number 75, targeting number 23 and why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you have infantry weapons in mind --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I have in mind a shot from so-called light weapons, as opposed to heavy weaponry.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The distance between these two points under the most ideal conditions is simply too big to be -- to use infantry weapons and to have this point hit by -- from an infantry weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know if along the trajectory ideal trajectory, that is a hypothetical trajectory which is represented by this red triangle, are there any topographic elements or structures which would be an obstacle to a direct hit from a light weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are structures which obstruct the view. There are buildings, there are houses, private houses, and taller buildings which obstruct the view. Besides, both parties to the conflict throughout the war put up screens made of vehicles, carpets, tin plate and so on, to protect their respective side from being seen or hit by the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, inside the red triangle and since the map does not provide that information, would there be any buildings, any structures, that is, obstacles obstructing the direct view?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there are such buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, did you yourself go to this place which is called 75, on the map, that is to the school?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And during the war, at whatever time, did you have from this school, could you see directly the point number 23 indicated on the map, if you remember? Could you see it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did come to the convent on a couple of occasions, mostly because of our medical corps which was on the ground floor. It was not safe to go to upper floors. They had large windows. The convent was hit by a Howitzer shell and two floors were also pierced vertically. So I did go there, but I did not go to upper -- to the upper floors. I would only be on the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. But then from the ground floor could you see 23, the point 23, could you see it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I couldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, we have seen that at times questions, hypothetical questions can be asked, so my question is as follows: Had you been on the first floor? I am talking about a possibility. Would you have been able to see point 23? Could you answer that question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What does this mean, that you cannot answer or that you wouldn't have been able to see it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't have been able to see that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. And from an upper floor, what would have been your answer? I think that the building has two upper floors. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not quite sure. But I do not think you could see it from the second floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. So your answer is that, according to your experience, you think that one would not be able to see it from upper floors? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object. Perhaps for the same reason, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This is -- you are asking for speculation, unless there are specific reasons why the witness would have the knowledge or experience. So let me just ask you: What made you believe that you could not see from the first or from the second floor point number 23?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I apologise for interrupting you with the question. But in fact the witness's answer was equivocal as to the second floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, he said --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: He said he did not think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You said that you did not think you could see it. So you were -- certainly, as far as the second floor was concerned, uncertain. Could you explain this on the basis of what you would draw these conclusions, because these are conclusions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will show you what I am talking about, to be on the safe side. The location of the School of Theology is lower than the rest of Nedzarici, that is, you go uphill towards Mojmilo and Alipasino Polje. Private houses which you can find here, around here, are mostly two-storey buildings. So if we look from the same altitude, from the position of the convent, that the School of Theology, any of the houses around it is at the same level, plus a roof. So it is yet another storey then. So they are about the same height, and therefore it screens off the view, it obstructs the view, you cannot look over them, probably from the third floor. But I cannot say about the third floor, but from the second floor, I am quite positive, because it is only logical.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. On the basics of logics, did you ever specifically measure the height of point 23?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am not talking about houses. That would be the next question. Do you know exactly what is the elevation level of point 23?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Point number 23, that point is for sure higher than the Faculty of Theology. I grew up in this area, and I know that area very well. It is possible to prove this in many different ways. You can, for sure, know if I am lying. There is some maps. You also have data that you can examine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say that point 23 is higher. Is it considerably higher than the -- where the ground where the School of Theology is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I couldn't really tell you if it was considerably higher. But with respect to the Faculty of Theology, when we look at here, the level becomes slightly inclined. So it goes slightly higher up. And as soon as you get closer to Mojmilo because of the hill, the inclination is greater. So it is close to the reservoir points which we discussed earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I would like you to go back to point 75. Could you please point the pointer on number 75 on the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No, leave the pointer on the dot, please, on the same spot. Thank you. Witness, with regards to this area that you are indicating right now, that is to say right or to the right of the Faculty of Theology, were there any buildings, any structures, and if so, at what distance with respect to the facade of the Faculty of Theology.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the question as translated refers to buildings to the right of the Faculty of Theology. And the pointer is, as I understand it, to the left. Perhaps I am mistaken. Perhaps that might be clarified if that is to the left or the right that Mr. Piletta-Zanin wants his answer to relate to.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like this objection to be rejected. We know very well -- we all know very well what is right and what is left. I asked the witness to stay on number 75. The right-hand side corresponds to west -- east -- sorry. I would have said that. But I think that this question is so clear. And I cannot accept such an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question is not clear. What is right and left always depends on the direction of view. So would you please clarify the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: To the east, please. Witness, have you heard my question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: My question was with respect to the east of the buildings, so you are showing to us now an area, you are using the pointer to show us an area. Were there any buildings in that area, and if so, what was the difference -- the distance of these buildings with regards to the facade of the faculty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The convent was here, but right next to the convent there were no bigger buildings or bigger structures or houses. Along the river here, the Dobrinja River, there was an alley of trees here in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Were there any other trees in the area that is within the triangle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you please show us where, with the pointer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you please do so.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right here there was a house. It was the house of the family called Sucur and it was approximately right here. Now, right there, was this line of old trees and here as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much for stopping.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, the witness showed us the presence of a house that is situated immediately above a dot to the right of number 75, that is, to the east of 75, and then using the pointer the witness showed us a treeline or tree barrier, if you will, situated right above number 75 and above the dot the black dot previously mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, Witness, were there any other constructions --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I just add something?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, for sure.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The south side of the convent, I am showing you this area now, was one floor lower. It was just right after the war, because the convent was so damaged, one floor was added after the war. So before the war and during the war, this part here was only composed of three storeys. So it was only a three storey-building at that time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Witness, would you please be a little bit clearer, if you may. What is the exact part of the convent which was one floor lower? Could you tell us what it is? Could you show us? Could you show us clearly on this map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness just showed the facade situated to the south-west, that is to say the facade representing Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the side if we -- which has a direct view on the area or the neighbourhood called the airport neighbourhood. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could we now talk about something else please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't think that it is necessary to produce this map because it was already tendered and I think that we were clear enough for the transcript. But I see Mr. Ierace on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I may be mistaken, but the description given by my learned colleague as to the southern wall of the convent, I don't know that that reflects the evidence. In particular, the words "which has a direct view on the area of the neighbourhood called the airport neighbourhood." I am not sure if the witness has said that wall had such a view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if I may, we were talking theoretically. This is a view, if we look at the map, but if you protect the wall, the facade, what is right in front of this wall or the facade is the airport neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then perhaps you say that "on the map this wall faces the area," which is a different thing whether you had a view or not. But I do understand that this is a mistake and the precision has been corrected now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Piletta-Zanin this witness has been scheduled for two hours. Yesterday you used 65 minutes. The Defence used 65 minutes. Today we used 55 minutes. So there is not much time left, I would say. Could you give us an indication of how much time you would still need? And let me just indicate to you that the Chamber has discussed that we will be rather strict on times indicated, especially after the experience of last week. Could you give us an indication how much time you would still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, do you know if there were any defence structures such as trenches situated around Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, have you ever seen people working on those trenches? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, when and where have you seen people working on those trenches?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area right across of my position, we called it Sevula Kuca [phoen], Cenex, it was destroyed after the war. Now this structure does not exist any longer. But this is where I would see them dig trenches and make fortifications. However, we know from the Serbs who were either exchanged or who had run across, those were imprisoned Serbs, so we never fired on them. We never opened fire on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When you say "these people who were digging trenches" you are talking about the people who were digging the trenches, is that it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Those were very risky areas because this -- and this is why they, those captured people were digging.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know or had you ever -- have you ever heard that those Serbs were either civilians or soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were civilians people.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object. Mr. President, again, for the third question in a row, the witness is giving information without giving evidence, without a proper basis for that evidence being laid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please create a factual basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you please tell this Chamber, what is your personal knowledge of this? How did you come to find this out? How did you know that those were civilians? Could you tell us how did you personally find out these facts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I will explain. People whom we would see dig trenches and make fortifications or fortified positions were people who were not armed and they were wearing civilian clothes. Furthermore people who were either exchanged or who had escaped were always called to go and have some discussions with the authorities in the police station. And they would communicate interesting data that were of interest for us, that is to say they were to tell us where the artillery weapon was deployed. They were able to tell us, for instance, where the army was moving, how they were moving, where they were going. And those people would testify as to what happened to them personally during that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you also told us that consequently you were not firing on these people. Could you please repeat what you told us say? I remember hearing something similar earlier.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We would not open fire on them for those same reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, with regards to your personal knowledge, do you know if the facts that you just described regarding Nedzarici, do you know if those facts happened somewhere else, those situations happened somewhere else on other parts of the line?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So far we have the witness saying that the escapees were debriefed by the police. We don't know how this witness learned that information from the police, whether it was on the media, whether someone told him that, whether the police told him that. And now the witness is being invited to speculate about what might have happened in other areas, again with no proper foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if you ask the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- something he did not observe himself would you always ask him from whom or by what means he got this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. This was my second question. I was just getting to it, Your Honour. Let me ask the first question please. Since Mr. Ierace made an objection, we would like this objection to be denied since he made an objection with regards to my question. And I believe that my question was perfectly admissible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think, as a matter of fact, that the proper way of questioning would be that you ask the witness whether, and by what means, he obtained any information on what would have happened elsewhere, and then the second question, what was the content of this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. But may I just ask my first question, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your first question was about the content, as far as I can see, and not about the source of knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. So you give me the permission, therefore.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you know if what you just told us, that is to say the fact that civilians were working on the trenches, if this happened in other areas along the line, and if you know so, Witness, how did you find this out? How were you made aware of these facts?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin you now combined the two questions. Mr. DP4, did you ever receive knowledge on similar situations elsewhere, and how did you get that information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I found out about this and about other areas because for a very short period of time -- I cannot remember his name exactly -- but if you want me to remember it, I will. There was a man who was a Serb, he was from Hrasnica, and he was doing some forest labour. He was digging a tunnel under the airport tarmac and he didn't stay there very long because he had psychological problems. Now with regards to the information and the people who were debriefed by the police, the escapees who would leave Sarajevo, those informations were communicated to us pending on the area in which those people worked. So it means that the people who were digging trenches around Nedzarici were -- gave statements and then this information would get to the Nedzarici unit through our chain of command. And then the commander of the company would come to tell us the relevant information -- the relevant information communicated to that person through personal knowledge of the person in question who communicated the information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand that the relevant information for the Nedzarici was related to you as a result of the debriefing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Through a personal conversation with that man from Hrasnica and also through statements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Reports. I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you know the name of the people or the person you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall the man in question, the name of the man. I am sorry. But during -- but when I come back, when I go back home, I can try to find him because he is in that area. So I may find his perhaps statement and I could communicate it to this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Was there somebody who was with him and can you tell us some other name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not with regards to the position I held.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, I mentioned a few people with you, were there any people with you who would be able to find or to tell us his name and not with him. Thank you. That is all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, is the Prosecution ready to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know what your first subject would be. If it takes more than five minutes, I suggest that we have a break now. If you have a subject that could be covered in five minutes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will proceed, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many were there in your company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In our company there was over 100 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What equipment, apart from rifles, pistols and machine-guns, did you and your fellow company soldiers have?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object to this question because this question implies undoubtedly the following fact: That these soldiers absolutely had other weapons in their position. If the word "if any" was added, it would have been acceptable. To me, it is just the way the question is formulated and this is why I object.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Indeed in examination it would have been a prerequisite to add those words but not in cross-examination, Mr. President, in my respectful submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact Mr. Piletta-Zanin, we discussed before leading questions. And one of the elements that would make a question a leading one would be that the answer is suggested in the question itself. That would make a question a leading one. This certainly is a leading question, but as we also have discussed before, leading questions are not impermissible in the cross-examination where they generally are in chief. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What weaponry, apart from small arms up to and including machine-guns, did you and your fellow company soldiers have, and let's say, as of December 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Other than from what you just mentioned because of course we were an infantry company, let's not forget that, we only had an anti-tank light weaponry. We had hand-held rocket launchers and hand -- that is to say, those cannons against anti-tank cannons.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were there any mortars in your company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my company, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Having regard to the frontline that you drew yesterday, and for the transcript, for the record, that is on Exhibit D7169, I take it that the former JNA barracks were near your section of the frontline. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were there soldiers outside your company operating at any stage between September 1992 and August 1994 from those former barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where my company was situated, so that is in the whole barracks, no other soldiers came there except that at one certain point in time there was a commandment in the upper wing and it was also the kitchen which served food to the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the commandment in the upper wing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The command of our company, our battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you drew the frontline yesterday you took it up to, but did not include, the Institute for Blind Children. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The institute used to belong to our company, yes. So it represented the border. It did belong to our company, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I notice Mr. Piletta-Zanin is on his feet, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, what I wanted to say is that my colleague is going to ask questions with regards to what the witness said yesterday. It would be fair to show the witness that he himself annotated so that he can check it and testify with the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think in general terms, Mr. Ierace, especially since the witness might not have in his mind specific -- with high precision what he marked on the map yesterday, it would be preferable to do so. The witness has now answered the question. I think we have to have a break anyhow. If you would like to ask further questions on the markings the witness made on the map yesterday, would you please provide him with a map. We will adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Might we start off in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will turn into private session. Or closed session, that is the same in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. It will only be for about five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are in open session again. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yesterday, you told us that the first commander of your company was Bozidar Cvijetic and he remained in that position, you think, until mid-1993. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You said that he was followed by a young man with the nickname Gasi. Do you recall his full name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When did he cease to be your company commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was there for about half a year. I cannot remember exactly because it was a very long time ago. And then until the end our company's commander was Mr. Ljubo Cvijetic, as I have already said.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do I take it, therefore, that Ljubo Cvijetic became your commander from around the end of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If my memory serves me well, that is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Before the break this morning, you said that at one stage there was a commander in the former JNA barracks in Nedzarici, and you went on to say it was the commander of your company, of your battalion. Was it your company commander or your battalion commander or both?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Be precise. Whom do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You told us that in the barracks there was a command post. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is. The command post of both battalion and companies, but not one in the same man.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did that command post operate from -- I withdraw that. Was that command post in existence in September of 1992, and if so, for how long after that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has just said that there were two command posts. So Mr. Ierace should be more precise and say battalion command, company command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did the company command post exist in that position in September 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So that's where Bozidar Cvijetic had his command post in that month. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did the battalion command post exist there in September 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many battalions were there in the brigade? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there only the one battalion operating in Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So that was the command post for the battalion commander for the whole of Nedzarici in September 1992, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Who was the battalion commander in September 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radivoje Grkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And when did he leave that post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards the end of 1992 or in the beginning of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Who replaced him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then we joined with the airport locality and part of Kasindolska in one and we became one battalion. And Svetozar Guzina nicknamed Seso then succeeded him as commander in that whole area?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When did that happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Early 1993. I can't be more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Who was the commander of that new one battalion?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that things are going through at night, but in case our possible additional -- cross-examination could we have the name of the commander clearly. We want to know who is this about. I am talking about line 41 -- page 41, line 22.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please slowly repeat the name of the commander who came in early 1993 on -- of which you said his nickname was I think Seso.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Svetozar Guzina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: To be clear on that, was he the commander of that new single combined battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were his headquarters also in the barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where were his headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of Kasindolska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the witness be shown map D1764.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On the map, would you please point to the position of those headquarters with a --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I think it is a blue pen, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Blue for the Prosecution, black for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You told me to point, not to draw?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No, no, that is correct. But would you now please take a fine blue point pen, fine blue pen and place a cross at the position of those headquarters.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps the ELMO can pan back so we can see the sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Would you please place the initials "HY" alongside that cross.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, just to the right of the headquarters we see a yellow road running up and down the screen. What was the name of that road in 1992? It passes through the number one that you wrote yesterday.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the highway from the airport to Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, did the headquarters stay in that position until at least August 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The headquarters remained in that place until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And for what period of time did that commander stay in that position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the end of the war, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, between September 1992 and August 1994, were there civilians living in Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes few, but there were because our numbers were declining.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was there any particular reason as to why the civilians were not moved out of that area, given your evidence this morning that all of the buildings in Nedzarici had been hit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilians by and large had nowhere to go. Because this whole area was exposed to operations and they preferred to be killed when at home than as refugees. Those people who stayed behind, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you understand that in the areas controlled by the ABiH, on the other side of your frontline there were also civilians living?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could assume that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the ELMO pan back, please. Is it possible for the ELMO to pan back. Thank you. Further. Further. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, a few moments ago you pointed out the highway that ran from the airport to Sarajevo. Would you please run your pointer along that road from the UN post up to where it joined the boulevard? In the other direction from the UN post that you marked yesterday, heading north.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, would you please move the pointer along that yellow road from the UN position as marked on the map up to the main intersection.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please stop there. All right. Now, along that road on the ABiH side of the confrontation lines, did you know there to be residents, that is, civilians living on either side of that road?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We didn't have any precise information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The question seems contradictory to me. Because first it is talking about the ABiH army's side, which should be to the east, and then answer by the two sides. Therefore, the question somehow seems to me contradictory. Could it be made more precise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree with you that the question started with the ABiH side and then continued on both sides. I do not know whether it would create great confusion. But, perhaps, Mr. Ierace, if you ask about the line, perhaps not use "one side" and "both side" in the same question. Although I take it that the witness would have understood that it is civilians living on both sides of the line. Is that how you understood the question, Mr. DP4?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with regards to the situation that prevailed on the lines that were further away from our lines meaning behind the enemy lines, we can only assess or infer things. I do not have any particular knowledge. But I can tell you with regards to the lines that were in front of me I was -- I could tell you it was the market, nobody lived there. And then the circle indicates new constructions that were right in front of us. So these were newly constructed buildings, businesses actually, commercial buildings. But they were not finished. And so I was not able to see on the other side. So I can only infer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please continue, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And what did you infer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I was quite clear. I can only -- or I could only assess or guess what was on the other side. But with regards to what was in front of me, I think exactly what was there, and I know that it was not inhabited directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You told us that you received orders to not target civilians. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: How many times between September 1992 and August 1994 did you receive such orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On many occasions. Because we were always told that we were being watched by the International Community like under a magnifying glass, and that we were always -- we were always accused of doing things. And this is why we had to protect our military pride.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you say you were always accused of doing things, do you mean accused of deliberately shooting and shelling civilians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were receiving the informations as to what we should not do. We didn't know what we were accused of. And we were told that we should defend our military pride. And it is obvious that we wouldn't do what a normal man wouldn't do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, you said a few minutes ago: "We were always accused of doing things and this is why we had to protect our military pride." What did you understand you were always accused of doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was referring to the fact that the medias could take advantage and say whatever they want to with regards to what was going on in that area. If something happens by error, one can always say that it was made on purpose. Or if there was a bullet, a stray bullet all of a sudden that was shot and it is quite possible that a stray bullet may kill somebody or may injure someone. And in order to avoid this precisely this is why it was defended to open fire if it was not necessary and only to reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was there any investigation carried out in Nedzarici in relation to the -- an allegation that civilians had been deliberately targeted by Bosnian Serb forces in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not receive information that somebody was hit somewhere, and this is why they were not able to carry out an investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So I take it that you are not aware of any such investigation being carried out between September 1992 and August 1994. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, you have told us that those orders were given during that period and you said, "on many occasions." How frequently? Once a week, once a fortnight, once a month?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At least once a week.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you ever receive any orders in writing during the period, that is, orders on anything between September 1992 and August 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No position of the line wherever there were soldiers at that post, nobody ever received a written order. It was always orally made.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you have command over any soldiers underneath you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So we are talking about orders given to you by voice at least once a week for some 23 months to the effect that you must not shoot civilians. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And I take it therefore that given you were armed with a rifle, that --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- when you used your rifle shooting across the frontline, you understood you had to be very careful not to shoot a civilian correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I will repeat: In the zone in question, there were no civilians. Our position was near the flower plant and it was just impossible to shoot in such a way that the bullet would go any further.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Were you in exactly the same position on the frontline for the entire 23 months between September 1992 and August 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Point again, please, to where that position was.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the installation. It is inside the nursery and that is where it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And were there some greenhouses in that nursery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So in your case, you could shoot safely in terms of avoiding civilians. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: But we did take the order seriously, so we did not shoot for any unnecessary reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Did you understand Nedzarici to be strategically a very important part of the frontline around Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We considered it to be an important position strategically, especially for us who grew up there and who were born there. So it was an emotional, it was an emotional importance for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Apart from the emotional importance to those who came from the area, it was a part of Bosnian Serb territory that extruded into the Bosnian government side, wasn't it? It was an outpost, if you like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am sorry. Are you referring to the Muslim forces in Sarajevo? Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What you would call the Muslim forces --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am trying to follow the instructions that you gave us earlier, so I would like to make an objection.
