The question, as it is asked by the Prosecution, has to do with a strategic notion. The question is, what was the strategic importance. But with regards to what was said earlier, it would be more adequate to first see if there were any strategically important places. This man was only a soldier, I would like to remind you, and this is why I think this question should be rephrased.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, could you please find a factual basis for the assessment of strategical aspects of the conflict by this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I rely on the fact that he was a soldier there throughout the period on the frontline and the nature of the frontline that is it extruded into the opponent's territory. And as we have seen, was exposed -- and from this witness's evidence alone -- was exposed on at least three sides.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mr. Ierace is not telling us how could this witness know any specific facts about the military art. He is asking some questions with regard to strategy, but strategy is something that people learn in military schools. For instance, he could ask the witness whether he went through a military training, for instance, if he took part in some war games, as they are taught in those schools.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, at least on your first question about strategic aspects, part of the answer of the witness was about emotional -- or how they experienced emotionally that and that might show some -- well, at least some confusion as to what exactly strategic position is. Could you please try to make it as factual.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I am sorry. The question I asked at page 49, line 13 acknowledged the witness's answer as to its emotional importance to him and then directed his attention to the extrusion of the territory into the Bosniak territory, and invited him to agree that it was in that sense, an outpost.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I can approach it a different way, Mr. President. I am very conscious of the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you would approach it in a different way, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please look at the map to your right which is Exhibit D1764. Please point to the Institute for Blind Children.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The frontline falls away to the south-west from that institution and also falls away to the south-east. Is that correct? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So here we have the Institute for Blind Children at the point of an arrowhead, if you like, into your opponent's territory. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could say this, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I don't know how it is translated, but are you familiar with the word "salient" that this was a salient on the frontline?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not say that it was like a nail. Our positions were surrounded from all sides. Now, if you are talking about that, I am not quite sure if I can answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Well perhaps it doesn't translate too well. For what period of time did your company control the Institute for Blind Children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout the whole period.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Why did you not draw the frontline, therefore, in such a way as to include those buildings?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Your Honours, I am not quite certain and would like to check something on the map. Just a moment, please. Yes Mr. President, this map seems to be slightly -- not to -- not sufficiently precise or insufficiently precise. We know that the institute is comprised of three buildings, and I have the impression that we cannot draw a conclusive evidence from in view of the map and in view of what is shown here. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, that is extraordinary given that it's a Defence map, given that the witness has just pointed to the buildings of the Institute for Blind Children, and given what the Trial Chamber knows. There is nothing wrong with that question and there is no room for misleading the witness by asking it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yesterday, you stopped drawing a line just before the Institute for Blind Children. The question of the Prosecution is why you stopped there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Without any particular reason, I was a little confused, the thickness of the felt pen was confusing me. And I thought it was more important to draw the line where it was most present. It is a 2-kilometre long area. And you could never walk along this line because you would just die. And during the war, I was not all that much present up there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber noticed that the opposite frontline of the ABiH forces was drawn a bit longer. So, Mr. Ierace, would you please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please take the blue pen the fine-point pen, and continue the northern end of the frontline, that is the frontline of your company so that it reflects the full length of the frontline that was operated or manned by your company.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. You have now extended the frontline through to the intersection of Aleja Bosne Srebrene Street and Lukavicka Cesta. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, did you go to any of those buildings between September 1992 and August of 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only once, escorted by the commander of the company during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was somewhere early 1995. I am not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The question was whether you went there between September 1992 and August 1994. Are you now telling us that you didn't go there at all in that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I am saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At any stage in that period, did you see amongst your fellow soldiers anyone with a rifle equipped with a telescopic sight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With regards to this line, no. Because it was visually impossible to hit something, any target, from the basement of the installations we were based at because we were defending the line.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Please listen carefully to the question and I will repeat it. At any stage in that period did you see amongst your fellow soldiers, and by that I mean soldiers anywhere in Nedzarici, Bosnian Serb soldiers, anyone with a rifle equipped with a telescopic sight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you were handed your weapon in 1992, you have told us that weapons were handed out by the Civil Defence which the neighbourhood community staff somehow procured, did you see then any weapons with a telescopic sight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The weapons handed out by the Civil Defence was old. Some rifles, M-48, for instance it is only later that I received an automatic rifle, sometime in the summer of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And is that a new rifle?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, what I wish to say at this point is the following: My objection goes back to the two previous questions, I believe it was not admissible. The first question began "at any stage of this period." When the witness clearly answered "no," he was asked a second question which goes as follows: When the Civil Defence gave you or handed you questions. It is the same question but asked in two different ways. And basically if the Defence did the same thing, I wouldn't think it would be allowed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is not quite clear to me to what question you are referring. I see one question starting with: "At any stage of that period." That is on page 54, line 2, is that correct? Or is there --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was referring to page 2, line 54, question 54. And I was referring to the next question on page 7, question 55. And I was also referring to question on page -- there is a question on page 12 so, I was basically talking about these three questions. The first question, question number 12, invites the witness -- or rather, the Prosecution asked the same question even though the witness answered, "no." So the Defence deems it is not an admissible question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am totally confused, I must say. Could you just tell me precisely what the content of the question was you are --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we may not have the same pages, but there is a question on page 54, I repeat, page 54, line 7. The question reads as follows: [In English] "At any stage in that period did you see amongst your fellow soldiers --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay that is the first question. And the second question was?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, and the second question is: [In English] "When you were handed your weapon in 1992" [Interpretation] A few questions lower. And then the same question is asked over again. Since the first question was saying: "At any point in time in that period, did you," and then after that the same question is asked in different words. So I believe that it is not admissible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, would you please respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: They are different questions, Mr. President. It doesn't canvas the same issue. It is a different aspect, that is whether in 1992 when weapons were handed out he saw then any rifles or whatever with a telescopic sight, whether or not they were handed to his fellow soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The objection is denied. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. I think I was asking you about the new rifle you received in 1992. Were new weapons distributed generally in 1992 at that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. New weapons were distributed to trenches. So I didn't always know what the others received. But with regards to us, we did not receive those weapons because we didn't have positions to shoot from. Because visually, we were impaired with regards to the Muslim soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Are you talking about rifles with telescopic sights?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were not handed those weapons because we couldn't use them. That's probably why we didn't receive them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. And are you saying that you would expect those rifles to go to soldiers who were in a position to use them, in other words, who had a wider view of targets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't guess these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: But you have made an assumption as to why you didn't get them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But I cannot guess, I could not tell you with certainty why somebody would not receive them and why others would. I am talking to you about what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now during the period that we have mentioned, September 1992 to August 1994, were there times when you observed artillery and mortars being used by your side to assist you in conflicts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Artillery was used in order to help or to answer when there was an artillery fired, fired. I can give you some examples, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That's all right. But the situation was that your side was outnumbered by the other side, correct? They had more soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is only an assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And in Nedzarici the frontlines were very close. I think you said yesterday, a matter of 50 or 70 meters, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You and your fellow soldiers when machine-guns and rifles, therefore, needed the support of artillery --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And therefore needed the support of artillery and mortars in order to hold the line, is that so?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of our lines there were some areas that were mined. And we were well fortified. It is only an exceptional circumstances when we were attacked heavily or when we had to pull out the wounded or the dead, we would ask through the commander of the company for some interventions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: From time to time --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Your Honour, I must say that I was not following the English text in the headphones. I must say that the way the question was asked on page 57, line 16, does not make any sense. On the one hand it was interrupted, and on the other there is no verb. I must say, I cannot follow very clearly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the witness was interrupting counsel for the Prosecution when he put that question. So I do not think that the Prosecution can be blamed for only finishing its question after the interruption. The question is finished on lines 19 and 20. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: On occasions, tanks would come in and offer you support. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Do you remember one of those occasions being on the 24th of September 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall the date. It was very long -- very long time ago. I cannot really -- I cannot really say which tank came out to fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In any event, the artillery and some of the mortars that gave you that support were located well back from Nedzarici, weren't they, not in Nedzarici itself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No that is not correct. In front of the convent or the School of Theology, there were mortars, 60 and 80 millimetre mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I appreciate that. Perhaps my question wasn't fully interpreted. I said artillery and some of the mortars. All right. So we have 60 and 80 millimetre at the convent or Institute of Theology. There were mortars at the barracks as well, were there not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of any mortars in the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Where else did you see mortars apart from the convent in Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am completely -- the interpreter's completely lost me. I am talking about 58:23, and I do not know what is it that the witness could have said in Serbian because I wasn't listening very carefully. But I know that in that place, the French interpretation talks with reference to Mr. Ierace's question about the convent. That is what I heard, the convent. I don't see it in the transcript, and I was not following Mr. Ierace. I don't know whether they were talking about convent or not, but I heard it in French. And that really sounds odd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I -- the witness answered: "In front of the convent or the School of Theology." Do I understand you well that you are using indistinctively the words "convent" and "School of Theology"? Is that the same for you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that seems to be rather clear from the answer of the witness. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace. And, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if it really is necessary to make an objection, could you do it in two or three lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Was the convent the only place that you saw mortars in Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yesterday you mentioned a particular weapon used by the ABiH which you pronounced as a Zolja. What is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is an anti-armour rocket launcher for a single time use.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, please look again at the map to your right. This morning we heard mention of the Airport Settlement. Would you please point to the area known as the Airport Settlement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And for the benefit of the transcript, the witness has pointed to a complex of streets, many of which are parallel, immediately to the north-east of that part of the map, identified as the Aerodrom Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It was suggested to you or it was suggested that the southern wall of the convent overlooked that area. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the lower part of the convent faces this locality.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When you use the phrase, "the lower part of the convent," what do you exactly mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you asked me about means this part that we already mentioned earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps you could point to it, that is the part you mean by "the lower part."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Do you mean the wall that faces south-west -- I am sorry -- south-east? The wall that faces towards the Airport Settlement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. The Airport Settlement and Dobrinja.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, it seems from your evidence this morning that the institute or the convent was obviously quite a target for the ABiH, that they repeatedly either hit it or tried to hit it. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is, like all the other places in Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, except that you have told us that there were mortars there, and you have also told us that it had a number of storeys correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that in the uppermost part of this building, and it is this part here, had four floors then a wing that was mentioned, which was a 3 storey wing. And this part here, lower, which housed the kitchen, the canteen and where our medical corps was during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Let me make sure I understand this. The northern corner was four storeys, the side facing south-west was three storeys. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And the side that faced towards the Airport Settlement had how many storeys?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Three.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So that was actually quite a good building to look over a large area, including into enemy territory, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because one cannot say that it is a tall building because it isn't and because it wasn't safe to go to the upper floors because they are not all that high, high up. And around us -- around it were six or 18 storey buildings. So as for the visibility, it was impossible to have a good visibility. Then, and I will show it to you here on the map, there were -- this is a row of buildings in Dobrinja V -- no, sorry -- here. Here you have a neighbourhood of private houses, there is a mosque there. And it also obstructs the view of this area. Here we have high-rise buildings and they can -- from them you can very clearly see this whole area, if you follow what I am saying. And there is also the distance that has to be taken out, which is a kilometre to a kilometre and a half to 2. One can measure it. One can look at the map scale and if one wants to establish the exact distance, one can easily do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, in the examination-in-chief it has been established that the witness never went up to the first or second floor, and that a lot of his observations are the results of his logic. When adding any questions in this respect, perhaps you could keep in mind to what extent it would assist the Chamber to have more logic and less observation. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. Might the witness be shown Exhibit P3259. I will keep that in mind, Mr. President. Perhaps while that is being done, I appreciate that much of that last answer will make little sense, given the witness hasn't described precisely where he was referring. But unless you wish it, Mr. President, I don't propose to bring out that detail. I will, if you wish it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether, on the basis of a map, where we all know that lines of view and sight are relatively complicated. If we just have to assess them on the basis of a map, whether that would be of great assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps the reason --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you think it is -- I asked you to keep in mind to what extent it would be of assistance. So if you would keep that in mind, proceed with the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps this will assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it seems to the Defence useful to put in the transcript what the witness showed because he was pointing at certain areas to say that there were structures there so that one couldn't see beyond them, behind them. And I would like it to be precise. We think that it should be in the transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the witness transferred mainly to the built up areas close to the dotted line the last part where it goes in north-easterly direction. If that would be a correct way of stating it for the transcript. Then please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, sir, I think the last few minutes you have been looking at two photographs in front of you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could it be put on the ELMO, if possible. Usher, could you please assist. Mr. DP4, we ask the photographs to be put on the ELMO so that we can see the same as you do. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps the usher could assist us with the last digits of the ERN on the photograph which is presently on the ELMO. Thank you. I think it is 4244.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In that photograph, do you recognise the convent, otherwise known as the Institute of Theology?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. Yes, you can see the top of the convent's building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please point to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The witness points to a white building which presently has a -- what appears to be a black circle placed on it. Is it black? Yes, thank you. All right. Would you now please, Mr. Court Usher, show the witness the second photograph. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, in the background of the photograph in front of you which ends in ERN 4245, do you see Nedzarici? Perhaps, sir, you could look at the photograph in front of you rather than the screen. That will give you a better view.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not clear. It is not clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Well, don't look at the screen look at the photograph. Do you recognise in the background, Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That might be returned. Those photographs can be returned. Thank you. And might the witness be shown -- excuse me -- the map that he was shown this morning. I think it is Exhibit P3728 relating to sniping incident 23.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you intend to tender that or would you --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, they already are in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I mean so you are using the original one and not the copies?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Oh, I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have been provided with copies, I take it for our convenience. No markings are necessary

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: No markings are necessary so I suppose it is the Defence copy of P3278. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, on this map, you see a dark green and light green parallel lines around Nedzarici, not entirely, but largely, do you see that? And again, sir, could you please look at the map rather than the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP4, on the map the colours are better, I take it. Your attention was drawn to the dark green lines and the brighter green lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In particular, would you look at those green lines in the area of the Airport Settlement. Do those green lines show the frontline positions in the Airport Settlement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might that be returned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can add that I was not at that frontline, and, therefore, I cannot affirm positively which was building to the left, to the right and who lived where.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, between September 1992 and August 1994 were there any ceasefires on your part of the frontline?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were several ceasefires on our side. At the time when ceasefires were signed we to be ordered not to open fire unless our lives were in danger.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You said that there were several ceasefires. During that period, would there have been more than ten or less than ten or about ten?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Less than ten.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was the longest period of ceasefire that you recollect in that period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of them lasted for a very short time because whenever there was a ceasefire, people would get relaxed and then invariably there were woundings and killings. What I am trying to say is that the enemy side did not comply with these ceasefires.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: My question is, what was the longest period of ceasefire and you said all of them lasted for a very short time. What do you mean by "very short time"? Hours or days or weeks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean one day or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for that. Now, you told us that you had some information that a Serb prisoner or a Serb civilian was involved in the digging of a tunnel. How did you come by that information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Concretely, as I have already said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, one needs to be more precise than this. A moment ago we were talking about Serb civilians in plural, so a number of persons, not as the question says, Serb civilian involved in the digging of a tunnel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see the single form in the transcript, and that is how you intended the question to be? So the question was about "a Serb individual" being forced to participate in digging a tunnel. Would you answer the question how this information got to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The gentleman concerned was assigned to us. He was a man younger than 55. So he was assigned to us as reinforcement as a replenishment. But since he was mentally disabled, we could not switch off the lights at night because he was traumatized. He was afraid of the dark. And a few days later, he left our lines, so this information I received directly from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When did he join your company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in late May that is, late May, early June 1995. And the whole period before that he spent in captivity in the Hrasnic prison and taken to do forced labour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did he ever tell you when it was that he came over to the side of the confrontation lines controlled by the Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right before getting to our line, that is joining our combat order, he had been exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So I take it that was sometime in 1995. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly, but if Your Honours need it when I go back, I can send you his name and another particulars. He lived in Hrasnica, worked at Famos and it was their settlement in Hrasnica. I saw him after Dayton at a new location in Serb Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, in Nedzarici, was there a tram terminal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear the question clearly. I mean, I couldn't hear the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I will repeat the question. I am asking you about something else now. In Nedzarici, was there a tram terminal?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was one such.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Might the witness again be shown map P1764.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While this is being done, Mr. Ierace may I ask you, we are close to the time where we usually have a break. How much time would you still need.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just a few minutes, Mr. President. I anticipate that I can finish this witness subject to a reflection over the break in the next few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, then please proceed and we'll then continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Could the ELMO be zoomed in.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please point to the position of the tram terminal in Nedzarici.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Now, have you just pointed to an area where, for a different purpose, yesterday you wrote the number "6"? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, number "6" marks students' hostels which are right beneath number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So the tram terminal is beneath the number 6. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Student hostels are beneath number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Student hostels are in the circle indicated by number 6. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... blue pen and place a cross to indicate the position of the tram terminal.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, as indicated by the map, was it the case -- I withdraw that. Before the war, did trams travel right along the boulevard into Ilidza and then turn around?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, some trams.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, that wasn't possible during the war. So did the trams within the city instead turn around in the vicinity of the Oslobodjenje building? If you don't know, please say so.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. There was no electricity so I think they were not in service, but I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So you don't know whether trams ran in the city between September 1992 and August 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Before the war, immediately before the war, were trams stored at the terminal? In other words was there a shed where the trams were kept on that spot or near that spot?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were parked on Grasova [phoen] which is where the shed was, where the tram depot was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Does that appear on the map above the word "boulevard" -- please look at the map. I think you can see the word "Gras."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The map will need to be moved. Perhaps the ELMO can pan back a little. Move to the right. Thank you. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So that is where the tram carriage was stored. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Witness indicates the area of the word "Gras."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Would you please circle that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Please put a circle around the tram terminal buildings or building.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: I am sorry. I could not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Nothing further, Mr. President. I would be grateful for it opportunity to confirm that immediately after the break. At this stage I don't anticipate any further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will then have a break until five minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. There is one further issue. I don't think it will take longer than a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, then, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Sir, you told us yesterday that the UN occupied two positions in Nedzarici. First of all, in relation to the position on the intersection, on the airport road, what was it exactly? Was it a building or a vehicle on the road? What?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was some sort of a control checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did it -- did you ever see it operating? In other words, did you see what they did, if anything, as vehicles went along that road, through that intersection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the main part they would communicate or get in touch with their own members with vehicles that were going from the airport towards Sarajevo. But I couldn't really tell you with precision what it was all about.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Essentially, it seemed to be part of the communications route between the airport and the city. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right. Now, the other position you marked on the map, I think you described it as an old people's home. Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And did you ever go there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: When were there UN people in that building? Sorry, I withdraw that question. If you never went there, how do you know about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about it from other members of our unit. And I was also able to see when they were bringing humanitarian aid for the tenants of the old people's home.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At some stage those tenants were moved out weren't they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no. A lot of them died, were killed, but I don't know if during the war they were moved or they had moved away or were transferred anywhere. There were many different nations living there together.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Did you ever meet any UN officials?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I suggest to you that if there was a UN post in that -- I withdraw that. Let's be a little clearer on exactly what you say happened there. I think you said you heard about it from other members of the unit, and you saw when they brought humanitarian aid in for the tenants. Is that all that you heard about the UN in that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard from the director, Milena Mucibabic she was a director of that place, that they were coming in to bring in humanitarian aid and food and other supplies.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: So you don't know what their function was in that building, apart from bringing in humanitarian aid. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only assume that they were a surveillance unit --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I am not asking you what you can assume. I am asking you what you know. In terms of what you know, it goes only as far as bringing in humanitarian aid. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that they stayed there, but I don't know if they only went there for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I suggest to you that if they stayed there, they only did so up until early 1993. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions. There is something I wish to raise in the absence of the witness. It need not be done now. It could be done at the conclusion of the witness's evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then perhaps we will first see whether the Judges have any questions unless the cross-examination would have raised an issue that the Defence would like to touch upon. Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, in answer to a question put to you by the Prosecutor, you mentioned that there was a mosque in the neighbourhood of Dobrinja. Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. With regards to that mosque, was it ever, during the period that we are interested in, was it ever shot at --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What can you tell us, sir -- I will rephrase my question again. And I withdraw the question as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The object was about the formulation of the question --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, it was to the substance of the question. Firstly, the mention of the mosque was not given in response to a question asked by me; secondly, it was not mentioned in the context of the issue that my friend now seeks to raise for the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you respond to that, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please use the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am terribly sorry. I do not know whether it was in answer to a question by myself or the Prosecutor but all I know is that -- rather, I believe, Mr. President, that it was following an intervention by the Prosecutor. I remember having asked that we put in the transcript the fact that the witness had shown small constructions, small buildings or family homes, and I described also the fact that he had indicated a mosque in the background. So, I do not remember if you recall this, but I believe it was following a question put to the witness by Mr. Ierace. And secondly, since the witness mentioned himself the existence of a mosque and since the Prosecution is saying that it was a campaign made to destroy cultural installations and objects, this was not the question --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object. I am very concerned about my learned colleague's choice to go into that sort of detail in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. How many questions would you have in mind, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are we talking about the mosque?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only one with regards to the mosque.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I am not telling you that it will go this way always, but usually an objection takes more time than a question. Please put the question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, what can you tell us, if you can tell us anything, about the physical state in which the mosque was during the war, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't hear that the mosque was ever targeted or hit. I do not know that fact. But it is certainly something that can be verified.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... question about the mosque, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Any other issue to be -- I saw in the transcript, as a matter of fact, that in response -- I don't know whether it is true or not -- but that you said I will reformulate my question, I will withdraw that question. So that is the reason why I thought we could be fairly quick on this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I pursue -- may I continue? I have some more questions to ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it depends on what subject. The mosque has been dealt with, I take it --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... what would be there that came up during the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. The Prosecution asked that two pictures be placed on the ELMO, those were two pictures showing some people linked to incident number 23. Could we please ask the usher to put these pictures back on the ELMO and I would like to ask some questions with respect to those pictures. We have two pictures, this one where we see -- may I please have them, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We have one overall picture and the other one is a close-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Very well. I would like to ask the technical booth to zoom in the area where we can see the convent, as much as you can. Thank you, thank you. That's it. Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, let's focus on the so-called convent. How many walls do you see here, that is my first question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One wall and we can only see something, a whitish surface, and it is the lower wall right here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. I am talking about the white building. Do you see here one wall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. But partially only.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Second question: Is this the floor that would have been destroyed during the war and consequently the one that was rebuilt later.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: That is a leading question, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Can you tell us --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- and contradicts the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That would be -- if you'd like to -- you put to the witness that a storey -- that a floor that had been destroyed during the war. Could you please indicate where the witness said that before continuing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I may search for the relevant passage, but from memory, I can tell you that the witness said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, it is in the presence of the witness we are not going to repeat what it was you who would like to have a direct quoting of --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I shall find it. In the meantime, would Mr. Ierace be so kind enough to tell me if what I said earlier with regards to mosque was right or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I am searching, but I am experiencing some technical difficulties with my system. I am not such a good operator, I must admit. So in order not to waste any time, I propose to ask the following question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, the building, did it have all its floors during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, what can you tell us, since you are telling us now that the building did not have all its floors during the war, what can you tell us about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the war, the convent was rebuilt, renovated. It became operational again. And one extra floor was added and also some other rooms were also added in the base -- on the ground level.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The wall that we see on this picture, does it correspond to one or the other of the parties -- sorry -- one of the other rebuilt areas or parts of the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not quite certain, but I think that this is the renovated area. So what is to the left on this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, with your leave, I would like to ask the witness to be shown the map covering incident number 23, but I would also like that the picture be kept on the ELMO or on the screen, that is to say maybe Mr. Usher can just superimpose the map --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, before that happens I would be grateful if we could have for the benefit of the transcript the description by you of the portion indicated by the witness as the renovated area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think it is of vital importance for the questions you put to the witness at this moment. So you perhaps could try to find it all and see whether what the witness testified about it at an earlier stage. I think it was during the examination-in-chief

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, what I mean is the portion just indicated by the witness just a few moments ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, the portion of the building in the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, he said, it is on page 78 line 20, "I am not quite certain but I think this is the renovated area, so what is to the left on this picture." At that point the witness indicated the left corner of the convent building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would say left from the circle? Yes. That's -- he indicated that it was the left part, that as far as he knew, that is clarified now for the transcript. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Could the map be put on the screen. [In English] All right. This way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you just told us that there is only one wall. If we now take a look from the place where the photography was taken which corresponds to point 23, isn't it true to say that we should at least see two walls, meaning one angle indicating two walls and one wall behind? This is if we take into account that we are talking what we can see from point 23.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Again it is a leading question. Secondly, it is a question that makes no sense, given what appears on the map which is on the ELMO by way of a depiction of the building, which is, at best, a dot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, I do take it that you are referring to the white large building and that -- could the parties -- could I just ask the witness to take his headphones off. [Interpretation] Is it possible that the parties may agree on the fact that from point number 23, it is possible to see not only one wall, but since there is an angle, that one could see two walls forming an angle? And when I am talking about a wall, I am referring to the Faculty of Theology. That building. Or belonging to that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps if the witness has his headphones removed and perhaps if he could not look at the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What we could do is in order to prevent the witness to -- could perhaps the -- Mr. DP6, do you speak or understand any French?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand French.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... headphones on, could he be put on channel five and could both parties speak English.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps the usher could press the video evidence button on the witness's --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I think that is the best solution, practically.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps it is suggested to me by one of my colleague Judge's that it is better that the witness leave the courtroom. Because it becomes too complicated and the risk of failures and complex solutions always involve a risk. Would you please leave the courtroom just for a short while.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In English] No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, might I invite you to look at as well DP1764, which is the other map that depicts this building in symbolic form. And when one compares them --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They are different.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: They are different, and therefore, it seems to me it is unreliable to rely on either, in terms of what one would expect to see in the photograph in terms of whether it is one wall or more than one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, on both shapes one finds at least two walls, one going from south-east to north-west, and the other one going from south-west to north-east. The difference is that in -- on the map specifically relating to scheduled sniping incident 23, the walls are coming together at the corner, where on the other map, they do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can there be any agreement on whether from such a distance you would certainly see more than one wall? On both sketches, I would think that you see at least more than one wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it seems there is a great contradiction here between the map. Whatever the map may be, we were talking about the map presented by the Defence or the map presented by the Prosecution and the picture also. The problem was raised, and the only thing that you should do is to see if this picture is a possible representation of what we can see from that other point. So that would be enough. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is not quite clear to me. Could you please repeat that last part of your -- I will try to change to French.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. President, what the Defence wishes to say here is the following: That of course it is not the same thing that we see the evidence presented, exhibits of the Prosecution of the Defence were not the same. On one picture we only see one wall whereas on the other map, if we see something, we should at least see two walls. We agree with this. We are satisfied with this proposition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... established that one sees only one wall? Can we take that as a fact. I am just wondering --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Present, I have one small request. Since I am listening to two channels and they are not always in sync. It is not also a channel in which you are speaking -- so if you speak to me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, did I understand correctly that you understand as it being a fact that we only see one wall? Is that what you are telling me?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am listening to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I only am trying -- the only thing I am trying to say is that there is a contradiction in the exhibits produced by the Prosecution. There was one picture that is supposedly taken from this part of the incident, and that shows only one wall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but you are telling us that this picture only shows one wall; is that correct? On the basis of what can we accept this?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The testimony of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I better understand you now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The picture only shows us one wall and my eyes also enable me to see only one wall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [In English] Does the Prosecution agree that we only see one wall?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President. And it seems -- perhaps this could be clarified that my friend is now disputing that the building on that exhibit marked on the photograph is the Institute of Theology. Is that in dispute?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, whether it is the position of the Defence that the white building with a black marking, circle marking on it, is not the Faculty of Theology? Is that how I have to understand the position of the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I am trying to say, and I shall not say anything more, is that there is a great deal of contradictions with what we can see on the picture and the presentation of the map presenting incident number 23. It cannot be reconciled. I do not know how to reconcile the problem. I don't if it's the faculty, the monastery or whatever it is but I know that these two do not concur. I don't know if the evidence was proven by the Prosecution, but one contradicts the other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is the position of the Defence. Now, what would you like to ask to the witness as the next question because that is what -- why we were asking the witness to leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I have only one and that will be my last and definitively last question. It has to do with the tram.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. No more questions about the Faculty of Theology. Then we could ask the witness to enter the courtroom again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your patience. There is one more question to be put to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I want to be sure about one thing. You were asked about the tram. And my question to you is the following, and very precise: Do you remember until when until when did you personally see the tram travel to and from Nedzarici for the last time? When was the last time that you saw the tram get to and from Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot remember exactly when, but shortly after the conflict broke out problems with electricity started on their side and on our side alike. So I suppose that it was right then that in 1992 they could not travel already, but I can't be quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. I have finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Judge Nieto-Navia has one or more questions to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you Mr. President. Could we put the map 1764 ... Would you use the pointer to point at the Airport Settlement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Now, with the green pen would you circle the area and put the letters "AS" for Airport Settlement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, could you describe the type of construction of buildings houses or high-rise buildings, what was the type of construction there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Airport Settlement where a low residential buildings, such as ground floor and one floor, and they were in rows. So these were low buildings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Now, can you see the dotted line going north-west, the one on the map, the one that you drew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: What was the type of construction there in that area where it says Branislava something. Are you following me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Yes, that area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, do you mean buildings on our side towards Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Inside, in the interior -- in the interior behind the Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Sorry. South of the road which bears the name Branislava.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nusica, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Yes, that area.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This area. In this area are again private family houses. As a rule, usually one-storey building, that is a ground floor and one floor above. Just one-storey houses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you. No more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Nieto-Navia also has a question for you -- I am sorry, Judge El Mahdi. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. [Interpretation] I would like you, please, if you remember, to tell me the following: You were talking about the issue of rifles with telescopic sights which was in 1992. Could you be more precise and tell us which month was it? Was it towards the end of the year or when or perhaps early summer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my reply when I was asked by the Prosecutor, I said that I did not see those weapons being distributed. So I cannot really say when and how they were issued, but we got new weapons in the summer of 1992 and then onward gradually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I am not talking about you. I am not talking about the rifles that you received. I was referring to the issue of new weapons which also featured the telescopic sights. And you said that they were also issued in 1992, perhaps I am wrong, so perhaps you could put me right in that regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry. But I just received instruction from my colleague. I do not know that this witness said that. Perhaps we are failed, but it would really surprise me if there was any mention of rifles with telescopic sights.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is page 56, if that helps you. And I would like to seek information --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much and my profoundest apologies. I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I can also be more precise and I can say that the rifles, that is this type of rifles, were not issued to them because in view of the positions that they held, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we completely agree and I was -- I was wrong. My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not say that this type of weapons was ever distributed in our area, and such weapons were not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not talking about yourself. I am not talking about your company. I am speaking in general.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In general in the area which I knew as far as I knew it, I did not see anyone being issued with such a weapon. Because in that area, it could not really be of any use, and I do not know whether and when it was issued to people in some other areas, so I can't say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have got one question for you as well that's about the Faculty of Theology. I read part of your testimony of this morning. You said, according to the transcript: "The south side of the convent, I am showing you this area now, was one floor lower. It was just right after the war because the convent was so damaged, one floor was added after the war. So before the war and during the war, this part here was only composed of three storeys. So it was only a 3-storey building at that time." That's what the transcript says about your testimony this morning. Is my understanding correct that one part of that building was added with one floor after the war, or was the whole building added with one floor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only one part of the building was added, Your Honour. You understood it correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And that was the part of the building facing, I would say, south-east, the map is still -- even if the building is not entirely correct on the map, but is that part of the building facing the Airport Settlement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you say a 3-storey building, do you mean ground floor and three upper floors, or do you mean three floors altogether, so ground floor and two upper floors?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, do I understand you correctly --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, a ground floor and two floors above it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So the -- this building, the southern part consisted of one ground floor and two upper floors after the war, that part that was facing south-east; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask the witness to be shown Exhibit P3279T. This photograph. And perhaps before doing so -- this photograph first. And that is the same series ending with 1A. So first the -- first the building from a distance. Yes. Mr. DP4, do you recognise a white building at a far distance just between the two apartment blocks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell me what building that is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the building of the School of Theology. Its tallest part which wasn't changed after the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This is the part which was not changed after the war, is that what your testimony says?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the other photograph be put... This is the same picture, but in more detail. Could you confirm that this part of the building consists of a ground floor and two upper floors?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object to that. Might I draw your attention to the fourth row from the left, at least as it appears on the computer screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. But let me just, Mr. Ierace, perhaps my next question might be about that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this building you can see the ground floor and three floors above it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is this the School of Theology?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP4 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your answers. The picture may be removed. I will give the other ones, two pictures, back to the Registrar. Mr. DP4, this concludes your examination in this courtroom. We know that you same from a far distance. You answered all the questions, both from the Defence, the Prosecution, and from the Bench. The Chamber is aware, having listened carefully to your testimony, that it certainly will have brought back in your mind also painful moments of the past. We thank you very much for having come to The Hague and to give us your testimony and I wish you have a safe trip home again. We will adjourn --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. But before I thank you, may I just say something. I remember the name of the man that I spoke about, and said that he had dug a tunnel under the runway. His first name was Milan. His last name still escapes me. But I would like to thank you and the personnel who took care of us during these last few days. And I hope that my testimony will help you and the truth. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, I do remember that you asked --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In the absence of the witness. But it doesn't require the witness to stay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It doesn't require the witness to stay. That is clear to us. Well, once again, thank you for coming. Mr. Usher, could you escort Mr. DP4 out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, if you could raise the issue very briefly. I know that the clock in this courtroom is a couple of minutes before clocks elsewhere. So we are close to a quarter to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, very quickly this witness gave evidence in chief that there was some sort of UN post in the old people's home which is on the frontline as it happens, drawn by DP6 for which he was the company commander. DP6 was asked no questions about that. The existence of UN posts was not included in the summary of facts, and so it came as a complete surprise by the Prosecution to hear this witness give that evidence, especially given that it had not been brought out by the Defence when DP6 was in the box.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Therefore, if DP6 is still in the Hague, in my respectful submission he should be recalled for further cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are we talking about DP6 --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In closed session I could indicate what the evidence is in relation to that in the Prosecution case and whether or not it had been put. That is, by the Defence, this account.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. First question: Is DP6 still in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not know. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does Ms. Pilipovic know?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do not know if DP6 left today. We could check in the Victims and Witnesses Unit, whether he left this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will ask the Registrar to check with the Victims and Witnesses Unit whether Witness DP6 is still in The Hague, and if so, of course, we still have to look at the objection. We don't have to hurry if Witness DP6 is not in The Hague any more. So we will first check that and see what should be done in respect of this objection. Is there any other issue to be raised at this very moment that could not wait until tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so. That cannot wait until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One, the Defence did not know what this witness was going to say. There are things which witnesses say like this without informing us about them previously. Secondly, the witness did not speak about -- one he simply said that the UN personnel were there. He knew that -- he said that he knew -- he knew that because he saw them bring in the humanitarian aid, and he believed there was also something else and that was it. He did not say he had a military observation post at that place. I mean, if every witness tells us every time what he knows, we shall never get out and if every time the Prosecution raises questions about this, we shall never get out of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to avoid too much emotion. One of the first things of course that had to be checked, whether there was a specific question in that direction, that of course would suggest that the Defence would have expected such an answer, but if it came up spontaneously, it might be totally different. We will look at it and we will adjourn now until tomorrow morning in this same courtroom. But not in the morning, we will sit in the afternoon tomorrow. So a quarter past 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
